Kedarnath Majumdar @ Kedarnath Mazumdar, aged about 56 years, S/o Late Vishwanath
Majumdar, Resident of Village - Jhikarhati, P.O. - Pakur, P.S. Pakur (M), District - Pakur
(Jharkhand) ... ... ... Petitioner Versus The State of Jharkhand ... ... ...

Opp. Party
-------
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Arun Kumar Rai

-------
For the Petitioner : Ms. Renuka Trivedy, Advocate Ms. Shabina Perween, Advocate For the Opp.
Party :Mr. Rakesh Kumar Sinha, A.P.P.

------
Order No. 07/Dated 13th September, 2024
1.

The petitioner is praying for grant of bail as he is in custody for allegedly committing offence
punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420, 467, 468, 471 of Ipc, in connection with Pakur Muffasil P.
S. Case No. 48 of 2024.

2.  At the outset, submission has been made on behalf of the petitioner that a false case has been foisted upon the petitioner and during course of investigation, no material has been collected which could show that alleged victims have ever deposited any amount with the petitioner and only oral assertions have been made by the alleged victims.
3.
He also pointed that no official affirmation is available on record which could show that fake account has been opened in the name of victims and amount has been fleeced away by the petitioner.

Lastly, learned counsel concluded his argument by making submission that petitioner is in judicial custody since 09.03.2024 and even no sanction has been obtained under Section 197 of Cr.P.C. and despite that learned trial court has taken cognizance of the offence which is not permissible under law.
Upon aforesaid premise, the prayer for bail has been made.

4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the State has submitted that petitioner was holding the post of Post Master and by using his post he induced number of victims and took their hard earned money and despite depositing in genuine/actual account of those victims, took money in his own pocket by creating fake passbook of post-office.

1 5.

He further contended that victims who are in double digit, belong to lower strata of the society and anyhow they parted with their money and there is every possibility that if petitioner would be admitted to bail then he will win-over and/or induce the witnesses, and also temper with other evidence as petitioner was holding the post of Post-Master, so there is also possibility that he would use his influence.

Lastly, it is urged that even otherwise, a supplementary investigation is pending,
petitioner should not be released on bail.
Upon aforesaid premise, the prayer for bail has been opposed.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned order.
7.

Perusal of the records transpires that one Divakar Mandal has opened a Rural Postal Life Insurance account in the year 2015 in Jhikarhatti government post office by the help of present petitioner having policy number is 856746 and a passbook for the same was issued.
8. It is further alleged that for the said policy, he used to deposit Rs. 1114/- per month with the petitioner and deposited 84 monthly installment total amounting to Rs. 93,576/-.

It is further alleged that, again in the month of January, 2019 he opened an another Postal Life Insurance Police and for that he deposited Rs. 3325/- per month and deposited 47 monthly installments total amounting to Rs. 1,56,275/- for second policy.

Later on, when informant went to Head Post-office at Pakur and inquired about the status of both the accounts then he came to know that Policy No.
856746 was opened, but no amount was deposited in that account by the petitioner.
Further he also came to know that second account was not opened, but the petitioner by opening a fake account had taken the entire amount from him.
Petitioner by playing fraud upon the informant, made forged entry in those passbooks.

9. Case diary reveals that there are as many as eleven victims who have come forward in the present case and Investigation Officer has recorded their respective statement during course of investigation and all the witnesses have stated in their respective statement that petitioner got opened their respective account and same modus operandi was adopted by petitioner what he did with informant.

It further transpires that all the victims had given their hard earned money to petitioner on the pretext of depositing the said amount in the account of post office and to get confidence of victims,
petitioner made forged/ fabricated entry in the passbook.

10. When query was made from the learned counsel for the petitioner that why and how, as many as eleven victims alleged against the petitioner with a motive to implicate him in false case, who (victims) have allegedly stated that they parted with money at the behest of the petitioner and petitioner opened fake accounts/accounts and made forged entries of deposits
, then, learned counsel for the petitioner unable to answer the query.
Possibility of tempering with the evidence as submitted by learned Addl. Public Prosecutor cannot be ruled out.

It also transpires that supplementary investigation is still going on and during this, Investigating Officer has recorded statement of one other victim Champa Dutta, whose husband deposited more than one lac rupee after opening of account by the petitioner but on inquiry they came across that fact that there is no record of their deposits.
Kedarnath Majumdar @ Kedarnath ... vs The State Of Jharkhand ... ... ... Opp. ...

2 11.
Considering the totality of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds that it is not a fit case to grant bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the prayer for bail of the petitioner is,
hereby, rejected.

12. However, it is required to be noted that if the prosecution would not able to examine all the victims within one year from the date of framing of charge then the petitioner is at liberty to renew the prayer for bail.

(Arun Kumar Rai, J.) Umesh/-
